import FormalConjecturesUtil


/-!
# Mean value problem

*Reference:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mean_value_problem)
- [The fundamental theorem of algebra and complexity theory](https://www.ams.org/journals/bull/1981-04-01/S0273-0979-1981-14858-8/)
by Steve Smale

Given a complex polynomial $p$ of degree $d ≥ 2$ and a complex number $z$
there is a critical point $c$ of $p$, such that $|p(z)-p(c)|/|z-c| ≤ K* |p'(z)|$ for $K=1$.


The conjecture has been proven for:
* `K = 4`
  [The fundamental theorem of algebra and complexity theory](https://www.ams.org/journals/bull/1981-04-01/S0273-0979-1981-14858-8/)
  by *Steve Smale*
* `K = (d-1)/d` if $p$ has real roots or all the roots of $p$ have the same norm.
  [Critical points and values of complex polynomials](https://doi.org/10.1016/0885-064X(89)90019-8)
  by *David Tischler*
-/

namespace MeanValueProblem

/--
Given a complex polynomial $p$ of degree $d ≥ 2$ and a complex number $z$
there is a critical point $c$ of $p$, such that $|p(z)-p(c)|/|z-c| ≤ |p'(z)|$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 12]
lemma mean_value_problem (p : Polynomial ℂ) (hp : 2 ≤ p.degree) (z : ℂ) (K : ℝ):
    ∃ c : ℂ, p.derivative.eval c = 0 ∧
      ‖p.eval z - p.eval c‖ / ‖z - c‖ ≤ ‖p.derivative.eval z‖ := by
  sorry

/--
The following weaker version of the mean value problem has been proven.
Given a complex polynomial $p$ of degree $d ≥ 2$ and a complex number $z$
there a critical point $c$ of $p$, such that $|p(z)-p(c)|/|z-c| ≤ 4|p'(z)|$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 12]
lemma mean_value_problem_leq_4 (p : Polynomial ℂ) (hp : 2 ≤ p.degree) (z : ℂ) (K : ℝ):
    ∃ c : ℂ, p.derivative.eval c = 0 ∧
      ‖p.eval z - p.eval c‖ / ‖z - c‖ ≤ 4 *‖p.derivative.eval z‖ := by
  sorry

/--
The following tighter bound depending on the degree $d$ of the polynomial $p$,
in the case of $p$ only having real roots has been shown by Tischler.
$|p(z)-p(c)|/|z-c| \le (d-1)/d \cdot |p'(z)|$
-/

@[category research solved, AMS 12]
lemma mean_value_problem_of_real_roots (p : Polynomial ℂ) (hp : 2 ≤ p.natDegree)
    (h : ∀ x : ℂ, p.IsRoot x → x.im = 0) (z : ℂ) (K : ℝ) :
    ∃ c : ℂ, p.derivative.eval c = 0 ∧
      ‖p.eval z - p.eval c‖ / ‖z - c‖ ≤ (p.natDegree - 1)/ p.natDegree * ‖p.derivative.eval z‖ := by
  sorry

/--
The following tighter bound depending on the degree $d$ of the polynomial $p$,
in the case of $p$ all roots having the same norm has been shown by Tischler.
$|p(z) - p(c)|/|z-c| \le (d-1)/d \cdot |p'(z)|$.
-/

@[category research solved, AMS 12]
lemma mean_value_problem_of_roots_same_norm (p : Polynomial ℂ) (hp : 2 ≤ p.natDegree)
    (h : ∀ x y : ℂ, p.IsRoot x ∧ p.IsRoot y → ‖x‖=‖y‖) (z : ℂ) (K : ℝ) :
    ∃ c : ℂ, p.derivative.eval c = 0 ∧
      ‖p.eval z - p.eval c‖ / ‖z - c‖ ≤ (p.natDegree - 1)/ p.natDegree * ‖p.derivative.eval z‖ := by
  sorry

end MeanValueProblem

findings.description: The hypothesis at line 84 compares every pair of roots, including zero. Tischler’s cited special case concerns the nonzero roots of the normalized polynomial, with p(0)=0 and evaluation at 0. These are different root-location conditions. For example, p=X−X³ has p(0)=0, p′(0)=1, and nonzero roots ±1 of equal norm, but the Lean hypothesis would equate the norms of 0 and 1. More generally, I proved in Lean that the file’s equal-norm hypothesis is incompatible with p(0)=0, p′(0)≠0, and degree at least two. Thus the declaration, which instead allows arbitrary z and unnormalized p, does not express this cited normalized special case.
findings.source_evidence: The mathematical review of Tischler, “Critical points and values of complex polynomials” (1989), Zbl 0728.12004, first describes the normalized quantity S_i=f(θ_i)/(θ_i f′(0)), then explicitly states the result when “all the nonzero roots of f have the same norm.” Read through https://api.zbmath.org/v1/document/_search?search_string=an%3A0728.12004 . Ng’s 2003 paper, p. 2, explicitly gives the normalization P(0)=0, P′(0)≠0: https://hkumath.hku.hk/~ntw/publications/paper13.pdf . Wikipedia’s shorthand omits the essential word “nonzero.”
findings.suggested_fix: State Tischler’s normalized version explicitly: assume `p.eval 0 = 0`, evaluate the bound at `z = 0`, and replace `h` with `∀ x y : ℂ, p.IsRoot x → p.IsRoot y → x ≠ 0 → y ≠ 0 → ‖x‖ = ‖y‖`. One may retain `p.derivative.eval 0 ≠ 0` or include its harmless trivial complement. To keep arbitrary z, impose the nonzero-root condition on `q := p.comp (Polynomial.X + Polynomial.C z) - Polynomial.C (p.eval z)`, rather than on p.

findings.description: The arbitrary complex evaluation point z needs verification against Tischler’s normalized real-root result. The available detailed summary discusses the result after reduction to evaluation at 0 with p(0)=0, whereas the Lean hypothesis concerns the roots of the original p and places no restriction on z. The usual normalization does not preserve that hypothesis: for p=X−X³ and z=2i, p has only real roots and p′(z)=13, but q(X)=p(X+z)−p(z) has the nonreal root 2−3i. I checked this in Lean. This rules out justifying the declaration by the usual normalization alone; it is not a counterexample to the asserted inequality. I could not confirm a separate all-z extension from the inaccessible original paper.
findings.source_evidence: Zbl 0728.12004 describes the normalized S_i=f(θ_i)/(θ_i f′(0)) and subsequently reports the real-root special case: https://api.zbmath.org/v1/document/_search?search_string=an%3A0728.12004 . Ng (2003), p. 2, explicitly states P(0)=0 and P′(0)≠0 in the normalized formulation. The cited Wikipedia page uses abbreviated wording that does not resolve this normalization issue.
findings.suggested_fix: Verify and cite an arbitrary-complex-z version if that is intended. Otherwise state the normalized real-root theorem with `p.eval 0 = 0` and evaluation at 0. An equivalent arbitrary-z presentation should require the roots of `p.comp (Polynomial.X + Polynomial.C z) - Polynomial.C (p.eval z)` to be real, not simply the roots of p.

status_issues.recorded: @[category research open], stating the positive K=1 conjecture.
status_issues.source_status: The current Wikipedia page reports a Lean 4 disproof of K=1 on 3 September 2026 by GPT-6 Astra in collaboration with Tom Adamczewski. It describes a normalized counterexample with p(0)=0, p′(0)=1, and |p(c)/c|>1 for every critical point.
status_issues.evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mean_value_problem#Disproof_(2026): “On 3 September 2026, Smale’s mean value conjecture for K=1 was formally disproved …”. This records what the cited page currently reports; I did not independently audit the claimed disproof.
status_issues.suggested_change: Check the newly reported disproof and update the research status/answer record accordingly. A negative answer should negate the universally quantified conjecture, not each individual fixed-p,z instance. This is a status update, not a misformalization of the originally posed conjecture.

reformulations.difference: The Lean statement permits critical evaluation points z and does not explicitly require c≠z; the detailed literature states the problem for noncritical z. It also divides the two norms instead of taking the norm of the complex quotient.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For noncritical z, any critical c necessarily differs from z, and `norm_div` identifies the expressions. If p′(z)=0, the additional Lean instance is true by choosing c=z: its inequality is 0≤0. In `/workspace/review/equivalences.lean`, `critical_point_extension` proves the exact equivalence for arbitrary p and real constant K between the all-z statement and the noncritical-z statement with c≠z.

reformulations.difference: As in the general conjecture, the Lean formulation includes critical z and uses the quotient of norms, whereas the quoted Smale theorem in Dubinin–Sugawa and Crane assumes z is noncritical.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Specialize the proved `critical_point_extension` equivalence to K=4. Noncritical z makes every critical witness distinct from z; critical z is handled by c=z. Thus neither totalized division nor the omitted noncriticality hypothesis changes the universal theorem.

sources_consulted: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mean_value_problem — statement, partial results, notes, and current “Disproof (2026)” section.

Tischler (1989), “Critical points and values of complex polynomials,” mathematical review by J. Illán González, Zbl 0728.12004: https://api.zbmath.org/v1/document/_search?search_string=an%3A0728.12004 .
Dubinin and Sugawa, “Dual mean value problem for complex polynomials,” introduction; LaTeX source: https://arxiv.org/e-print/0906.4605 .
Ng and Zhang, “Smale’s mean value conjecture for finite Blaschke products,” introduction and references; LaTeX source: https://arxiv.org/e-print/1609.00170 .
Crane, “Mean Value Conjectures for Rational Maps,” introduction and normalization discussion; LaTeX source: https://arxiv.org/e-print/math/0411604 .
Jatar and Ng, “Smale’s Mean Value Conjecture and its Dual Conjecture for Complex Polynomials,” introduction; LaTeX source: https://arxiv.org/e-print/2608.27047 .
Tischler, “Perturbations of critical fixed points of analytic maps,” Astérisque 222 (1994), especially pp. 407–410: https://www.numdam.org/item/AST_1994__222__407_0.pdf .
Ng, “Smale’s mean value conjecture for odd polynomials” (2003): https://hkumath.hku.hk/~ntw/publications/paper13.pdf .

Hinkkanen and Kayumov, “On Critical Values of Polynomials with Real Critical Points,” publisher abstract and references: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00365-009-9079-6 ; also its mathematical review, Zbl 1210.30002.

Beardon, Minda and Ng, “Smale’s mean value conjecture and the hyperbolic metric,” author-posted PDF, introduction and normalization section; text extraction was partly garbled: https://hkumath.hku.hk/~ntw/publications/paper10.pdf .
Hayman and Lingham, “Research Problems in Function Theory,” Chapter 4 passages mentioning Smale; LaTeX source: https://arxiv.org/e-print/1809.07200 .
Smale, “Mathematical problems for the next century,” Springer bibliographic/reference page only; full text unavailable: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF03025291 .
Córdova and Ruscheweyh, “Subordination of polynomials,” mathematical review, Zbl 0736.30018.

Bibliographic lookup pages: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smale%27s_problems ; https://math.berkeley.edu/~smale/biblio/biblio.html ; https://hkumath.hku.hk/~ntw/publications.html . Crossref, OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar metadata for the cited papers were also checked to locate accessible copies.
could_not_verify: MeanValueProblem.mean_value_problem_of_real_roots: the exact scope of Tischler’s real-root theorem, particularly whether it covers arbitrary complex evaluation points for the original real-rooted polynomial, could not be settled from the accessible sources. The failure of the ordinary normalization to preserve the hypothesis is proved, but it does not refute a possible separately established extension. See the qualified finding.
review.notes: All four declarations and the relevant Mathlib definitions were inspected. Successful scratch checks are in `/workspace/review/equivalences.lean`, `quadratic.lean`, and `root_conditions.lean`. They establish the critical-point equivalence, degree-convention equivalence, quadratic boundary cases, existence of critical points, and the root-condition witnesses/incompatibility. The named experimental proofs have no `sorryAx` dependency. The degree-dependent subtraction and division elaborate in ℝ, not ℕ; zero/constant/linear polynomials are excluded. The unused K parameter is semantically harmless. Publisher access prevented reading the original Smale (1981) and Tischler (1989) full texts; the general statements were corroborated in accessible literature, and Tischler’s nonzero-root qualification was checked in its mathematical review. Repository-related web links were not followed, and the target file was left unchanged.

submission.summary: Restated Tischler’s equal-norm case at the origin with p(0)=0 and p′(0)≠0, restricting the norm comparison to nonzero roots. Updated the theorem docstring and module summary. Left the questionable real-root variant and all other declarations unchanged; compilation succeeded with only the permitted sorry warnings.

    (hp0 : p.eval 0 = 0) (hp' : p.derivative.eval 0 ≠ 0)
